title: European warrior-monks and military-religious traditions
scope: European traditions and European-based military-religious orders; distinguishes individual combatant-monks from members of religious military orders and from legendary or disputed figures.

labels.documented-order: A historically attested religious-military institution; does not mean every member was ordained or a monk.
labels.individual-attested: A named individual associated with military action and a religious/monastic identity in historical tradition; degree of contemporary corroboration varies.
labels.tradition-or-legend: A figure or episode preserved substantially through later ecclesiastical, literary, or national tradition.
labels.adjacent-not-warrior-monk: Relevant military-religious or martial-monastic context, but should not be called a warrior-monk without qualification.

cautions: The modern phrase 'warrior monk' is an imperfect umbrella term. Many Latin military-order members were lay brothers under religious vows, not ordained monks.
Do not infer direct combat participation from membership in an order.
Separate contemporary/near-contemporary evidence from later hagiography, chronicles, national memory, and modern social-media claims.

Eastern Orthodox monasticism generally did not develop the same institutional military-order model as Latin Christendom; Orthodox warrior-saint and monastic-combatant traditions need their own evidence standards.
The list is an expandable research inventory, not a claim to be exhaustive.

nodes.name: Knights Templar
nodes.summary: Latin religious military order whose brothers lived under a rule and served militarily; members included knights and non-knightly brothers.
sources: Cambridge medieval histories on military orders
Sam Zeno Conedera, Ecclesiastical Knights (2015)
nodes.research_action: Map European commanderies separately from battle participation.

nodes.name: Hospitallers of St John / Order of St John
nodes.summary: Originated as a hospital brotherhood and later became a military order; military activity is attested from the 12th century.
sources: Cambridge medieval histories on military orders
Catholic Encyclopedia, The Military Orders (use critically)
nodes.research_action: Distinguish hospital function, landholding, naval forces and combatants by period.

nodes.name: Teutonic Order
nodes.summary: German religious military order combining religious life, military service and hospital traditions; later major actor in the Baltic.
sources: Cambridge, The New Cambridge Medieval History: Military Orders in the Baltic
nodes.research_action: Separate Holy Land origins from Baltic campaigns and later state-building.

nodes.name: Order of the Holy Sepulchre
nodes.summary: Religious order connected with the Holy Sepulchre; its medieval military character and later forms need period-specific treatment.
sources: Scholarly histories of crusading and military orders
nodes.research_action: Verify exact medieval statutes and distinguish later chivalric identity.

nodes.name: Order of Santiago
nodes.summary: Iberian ecclesiastical knighthood associated with frontier warfare, protection and religious life.
sources: Sam Zeno Conedera, Ecclesiastical Knights (2015)
nodes.research_action: Capture rules, vows, marriage rules by period, and local branches.

nodes.name: Order of Calatrava
nodes.summary: Cistercian-influenced military order created to hold the frontier fortress of Calatrava.
sources: Sam Zeno Conedera, Ecclesiastical Knights (2015)
Scholarly histories of the Reconquista
nodes.research_action: Trace Cistercian rule influence and institutional links.

nodes.name: Order of Alcántara (St Julian of Pereiro)
nodes.summary: Iberian frontier order that developed from the brotherhood of St Julian of Pereiro.
sources: Sam Zeno Conedera, Ecclesiastical Knights (2015)
nodes.research_action: Verify foundation chronology against primary and scholarly sources.

nodes.name: Order of Avis (formerly Évora)
nodes.summary: Portuguese military-religious order associated with frontier defense and Cistercian traditions.
sources: Scholarly histories of Portuguese military orders
nodes.research_action: Document relationship to Calatrava and changes in rule/status.

nodes.name: Order of Montesa
nodes.summary: Crown of Aragon military order established after the suppression of the Templars and used to assume some of their regional functions.
sources: Scholarly histories of Iberian military orders
nodes.research_action: Verify institutional transfer of assets and personnel.

nodes.name: Livonian Brothers of the Sword
nodes.summary: Military order active in the Baltic crusading frontier, later incorporated into the Teutonic Order.
sources: Cambridge, The New Cambridge Medieval History: Military Orders in the Baltic
nodes.research_action: Track merger and distinguish order members from allied crusaders.

nodes.name: Order of Dobrzyń
nodes.summary: Small religious military order formed on the northeastern European frontier and later absorbed by the Teutonic Order.
sources: Scholarly histories of Baltic military orders
nodes.research_action: Seek primary evidence for membership, campaigns and short institutional life.

nodes.name: Order of Saint Lazarus
nodes.summary: Leper hospital order with a complex and debated military role; should not be represented as uniformly a combat order.
sources: Scholarly histories of crusading and hospitaller orders
nodes.research_action: Classify by period and distinguish hospital brothers from military contingents.

nodes.name: Other Iberian and regional military-religious brotherhoods
nodes.summary: Research bucket for smaller or short-lived orders including Mountjoy, Monfragüe, Santa María de España, Faith and Peace, Militia of Jesus Christ and other regionally attested bodies; each requires separate verification.
sources: Scholarly catalogues of medieval military orders
Conedera (2015)
nodes.research_action: Split each institution into a separate node only after dates, statutes and sources are confirmed.

nodes.name: Alexander Peresvet
nodes.summary: Monastic warrior associated with the Battle of Kulikovo in Orthodox and Russian historical memory; details of the duel with Chelubey are preserved prominently in later narrative tradition.
sources: Zadonshchina
Skazanie o Mamaevom poboishche; compare critically
nodes.research_action: Source-by-source chronology and textual comparison; do not label all duel details contemporary fact.

nodes.name: Andrei Oslyabya
nodes.summary: Monastic figure associated with Peresvet and the Kulikovo tradition; biographical details and precise role require source criticism.
sources: Orthodox hagiographic tradition
Medieval Rus' chronicles; verify individually
nodes.research_action: Find earliest attestations and distinguish later hagiography from contemporary records.

nodes.name: Battle of Kulikovo
nodes.summary: Major battle in the formation of Muscovite historical memory; later accounts shape the warrior-monk narrative.
sources: Zadonshchina
Medieval Rus' chronicles
Skazanie o Mamaevom poboishche
nodes.research_action: Compare chronology and claims across the earliest available texts.

nodes.name: Joan of Arc
nodes.summary: Religious visionary and military leader, but not a monk or member of a military religious order; included as a comparison case, not as a warrior-monk.
sources: Trial records and modern critical biographies
nodes.research_action: Use as a contrast case to prevent category drift.

nodes.name: Hungarian and Central European royal-warrior saints
nodes.summary: Comparison category for Christian rulers later venerated as saints; kings and soldier-saints are not automatically monastic combatants.
sources: Regional hagiography and critical biographies
nodes.research_action: Add named individuals only where monastic status and military activity are separately evidenced.

nodes.name: European martial-monastic comparison cases
nodes.summary: Research queue for late antique soldier-saints, Orthodox warrior-saints, crusading lay brothers, monastic chroniclers present at sieges, and national heroic traditions. These categories must not be collapsed into a single identity.
sources: Regional primary sources and specialist scholarship required
nodes.research_action: Build country-by-country source register; add names only with a traceable attestation.

source_register.title: The New Cambridge Medieval History: Military Orders in the Baltic
source_register.use: Academic overview of Baltic military orders.

source_register.use: Later narrative tradition; must be contrasted with earlier witnesses.
